sentences.text: The prayer in the writ petition is made for quashing of the entire criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 27.03.2023 in connection with Bhawnathpur P.S. Case No.63 of 2022 pending in the Court of learned SDJM, Nagar Untari in the district of Garhwa.
3. The complaint case was filed alleging therein that she was married to one Rajesh Roshan as per Hindu rites and customs on 06.06.2014 at Bhawnathpur, Garhwa.

At the time of marriage her father had given Rupees twenty lakh in cash, gold chain, gold bracelet and gold ring to her father-in-law,
Kumar Satyendra Narayan Singh and her husband Rajesh Roshan.

After marriage, she stayed with her husband at her matrimonial village Kachra happily for two months and thereafter she came to the flat situated at Kantatoli, Ranchi with her husband and in-laws where they started torturing her and would say that she was taller than their son and was not fit for their son.

It was further alleged that in the year 2015 she became pregnant and husband started forcing her to have abortion for which she did not agree, then her mother-in-law, father-in-law and sister-in-law assaulted her in the month of August in the flat at Ranchi and she was forced to keep standing without food and water the whole night.
In the morning when her father and uncle came to Ranchi, they were told by her father-in-law to give Rupees five lakh as dowry then his son would not assault and abuse her.
Her father refused to give dowry then her father-in-law --2-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 674 of 2023 said that if Rupees five lakh is not given they will kill his daughter and would throw her.
They ousted the informant and as such she came to her parental house with her father.

It was further alleged that her husband came to Bhawnathpur several times before the birth of her son and would abuse her and would ask her for Rupees five lakh as dowry which was being demanded by his parents.
On 08.01.2016 she gave birth to a son at Daltonganj Hospital, the expenses of which was borne by her father.
She stayed at her parental house for six months and after great pursuation by her father, her husband came on 01.07.2016 and took the respondent to her matrimonial house.
After reaching there her in laws again demanded Rupees five lakh.

In April 2017 she was badly assaulted by her husband, mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law, brother- in-law and his wife and she was thrown out of the flat with her son and then she came to Bhawnathpur.

In the month of October 2020 her father sold the land at his ancestral village and gave Rupees five lakh to Kumar Satyendra Narayan Singh who after receiving the amount said he will see what has to be done.

On 17.12.2021, the respondent reached her matrimonial house at Kachra and after several request she was allowed to enter the house but she was abused and threatened of dire consequences by the accused persons.
After 17.12.2021 inspite of her best efforts she could not stay with her husband and in-laws.

On 09.01.2022 her husband took her and their son to Flat No. 101, Doranda,
Ranchi but then --3-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 674 of 2023 her husband would come late everynight drunk and would assault the respondent and her son.
On 28.01.2022 the respondent and her son were assaulted by her husband, brother-in-law, his wife and was locked in a room.
They called her father and other family members and she was thrown out of her matrimonial house on 29.01.2022 and she was threatened if she comes back, she would be killed.

It was further alleged that her husband is M.B.A. passed but they do not want the respondent no. 4 to study and as such they have kept all her original Rinki Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170811793/
2 certificates with them.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioner No.1 is the brother-in-law and petitioner No.2 is the sister-in-law of the respondent No.4 and both are residing separately and the case has been registered under Section 498A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
She submits that there are general and omnibus allegations against the petitioners and the learned Court has been pleased to take cognizance.
On this ground, she submits that maliciously this case has been filed so far these petitioners are concerned and in view of that the prayer made in the writ petition may kindly be allowed.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent State submits that the said complaint was converted under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. in light of the direction of the learned Court pursuant to that the FIR was registered and charge-sheet was submitted and the cognizance was taken.

Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.4 opposes the prayer and submits that in paragraph No.7 of the complaint petition there is direct allegation against the petitioners and in view of that the case is made out, as such this Court may not exercise this power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
He submits that what has been argued by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that can be a subject matter of trial only.

7. In view of above submission of learned counsel appearing for the parties, the Court has gone through the materials on record and finds that it is an admitted position so far these petitioners are concerned they are the brother-in-law and sister-in-law of the respondent No.4.

8. Looking into the contents of the complaint which was converted into FIR there are general and omnibus allegation against the accused persons and these petitioners are said to be residing separately and only a bald allegation is made out against the petitioners in paragraph No.7 of the petition and if such a situation is there the case of the petitioner is covered in light of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and Anr. reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 wherein the Supreme Court has deprecated to implicate the distant relatives if the case is arising out of the matrimonial dispute.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In the case of K. Subba Rao v. The State of Telangana, reported in (2018) 14 SCC 452 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has further observed that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against --5-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 674 of 2023 the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: K. Subba Rao v. The State of Telangana, reported in (2018) 14 SCC 452
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Recently Hon'ble the Supreme Court has dealt with a situation where the High Court had refused to quash the FIR registered for various offences, including Section 498A of IPC in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam v. State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599 wherein it has been held that the issue is required to determine as to whether allegations made against in-laws were Rinki Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170811793/
3

sentences.text:
general and omnibus allegation based on that matter can be quashed or not and it was held that if general and omnibus allegations are made against the distant relatives the cases are required to be quashed.
11.

In view of the above facts, reasons and analysis to allow the proceeding to continue, so far these petitioners are concerned will amount to abuse of process of law, accordingly the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Bhawnathpur P.S. Case No.63 of 2022, pending in the Court of learned SDJM, Nagar Untari in the district of Garhwa, so far these petitioners are concerned is hereby quashed.
12. This petition is allowed in above terms and disposed of.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.)
Sangam/
